documents.title: Press Release - CPCL Financial Performance For The Quarter And Half Year Ended 30.09.2026
Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Press Release / Media Release

analysis.summary: Chennai Petroleum Corporation Limited reported stellar operational and financial performance for Q4 and FY26, achieving the highest-ever crude throughput of 11.71 MMT, which is 112% of installed capacity. The gross refining margin (GRM) for FY26 stood at $9.2 per barrel, with Q4 GRM at $13.75 per barrel. Management highlighted comfortable leverage with a debt-equity ratio of 0.18 and active progress on key growth projects such as Group 2 and Group 3 LOBS and retail outlets. The board recommended a final dividend of INR54 per share, taking the total dividend for the year to INR62 per share. Management stated that CPCL achieved a crude throughput of 10.45 MMT (99.5% of installed capacity) for FY 2024-25 and highlighted a full-year GRM of $4.22 per barrel.

demand_outlook.claim: The southern market for motor spirit shows a clear shortfall where production is less than demand by close to 20 TMT per month.
demand_outlook.quote: MS in southern market, there is a clear shortfall so, the production is less than demand.

demand_outlook.claim: Motor spirit demand growth in the southern market is projected around 4% to 5%, while HSD is projected at 3%.
demand_outlook.quote: Like MS, they are projecting 6% and here we see around 4%-5%. HSD we see at 3% growth forecast, as against 2.5% odd here.

capex_expansion.claim: The company stated that project execution for Group 2 and Group 3 LOBS has started in full swing with all approvals in place.
capex_expansion.quote: Some of the important projects that we'll be taking up is Group 2, Group 3 LOBS for which all approvals are in place and the project execution has started in full swing.

capex_expansion.claim: The retail outlet endeavor involving 300 licenses has started, and commissioning will occur during the financial year '26-'27.
capex_expansion.quote: Even our retail outlet endeavor for which we had taken 300 licenses has started. And this year, that is '26-'27, we'll see a lot of commissioning out of them.

capex_expansion.claim: The LOBS project is budgeted at INR1,600 crores and the retail outlet project at INR400 crores.
capex_expansion.quote: LOBS project, Group 2, Group 3 LOBS project is INR1,600 crores. The retail outlet project is INR400 crores.

capex_expansion.claim: The revised capital cost for the Cauvery basin refinery project is Rs. 36,354 crores with a 25:75 equity holding between CPCL and Indian Oil.
capex_expansion.quote: The revised capital cost is at Rs. 36,354 crores with a 25:75 equity holding between CPCL and Indian oil respectively.

capex_expansion.claim: CPCL spent Rs. 673 crores as capex for the current financial year.
capex_expansion.quote: On the CAPEX front, in the current year, we have spent Rs. 673 crores as CAPEX for the current year.

capex_expansion.claim: The new refinery project capacity is approximately 9 million metric tons with a 6% polypropylene petrochemical intensity.
capex_expansion.quote: The new refinery capital cost is Rs 36,000 Crore approximately, 9 million metric ton capacity and petrochemical intensity of 6% and which is PP, polypropylene.

margins_costs.claim: The gross refining margin for quarter 4 was $13.75 per barrel.
margins_costs.quote: The GRM for quarter 4 was $13.75 barrel as compared to Singapore benchmark of $8.70 per barrel, which again reiterates that all these efficiencies are constant, continuous and are being sustained over each period.

margins_costs.claim: The core GRM for the fourth quarter was reported at $10.3 per barrel.
Foreign exchange loss for the quarter was approximately INR200 crores and for the full year around INR350 crores.
margins_costs.quote: For the quarter, it would be for the quarter, it is approximately INR 200 crores,. And for the whole year, it will be around INR350 crores.

margins_costs.claim: The full year GRM for 2024-25 was $4.22 per barrel compared to $8.64 per barrel in the previous year.
margins_costs.quote: The GRM for 2024-25 for a full year basis is $4.22 per barrel as compared to the previous year $8.64 per barrel, but if you compare it to Singapore benchmark which was $3.79 per barrel in the current year, we have performed better.

margins_costs.claim: The fuel and loss for the year as a whole came down to 8.51%.
margins_costs.quote: I must place it that if you remember our Energy Indexes and our Fuel and Loss Indexes were quite high 2-3 years back and we went to a roadmap where we said on a sustained basis, we will bring it down to very efficient levels and in that context, the fuel and loss has come down to 8.51% for the year as a whole.

margins_costs.claim: Inventory gain for the fourth quarter was $0.66 per barrel, amounting to Rs. 125 crores.
margins_costs.quote: Yes, the inventory gain is not very significant for the quarter. It is only $ 0.66 per barrel. And in absolute rupee terms, it is Rs. 125 crores only.

margins_costs.claim: The operating expenditure net was 1,085 Crore for 2022-23, 1,215 Crore for 2023-24, and 945 Crore for 9M 2024-25.
CPCL reported GRM was $11.91/bbl in 2022-23, $8.64/bbl in 2023-24, and $3.40/bbl in 9M 2024-25.

orders_capacity.claim: CPCL achieved the highest ever crude throughput of 11.71 million metric tons, equivalent to 112% of installed capacity.
orders_capacity.quote: CPCL achieved a highest ever crude throughput of 11.71 MMT, million metric ton, which equivalents to 112% of installed capacity, breaking records of our previous best of 11.64 MMT achieved in financial year 2023-'24.

orders_capacity.claim: Crude throughput for the fourth quarter reached 2.93 MMT, representing 111% of installed capacity.
orders_capacity.quote: In quarter 4 of the current financial year, CPCL achieved a crude throughput of 2.93 MMT, which is also 111% of installed capacity.

orders_capacity.claim: CPCL achieved a crude throughput of 10.45 MMT, which is equivalent to 99.5% of installed capacity.
orders_capacity.quote: CPCL achieved a crude throughput of 10.45 MMT, equivalent to 99.5% of our installed capacity and this must be seen with respect to the turnaround that has happened during the year

orders_capacity.claim: The Manali Refinery has an installed capacity of 10.5 MMTPA.
Crude throughput was 11,316 TMT in 2022-23, 11,642 TMT in 2023-24, and 7,480 TMT in 9M 2024-25.

capital_allocation.claim: The gross debt-to-equity ratio stands at 0.18 compared to 0.39 previously.
capital_allocation.quote: Our leverage position now stands at 0.18. Our debt equity stands at 0.18 at a gross level as compared to 0.39 last year.

capital_allocation.claim: Gross borrowings are INR1,900 crores while net borrowings stand at INR973 crores with a net debt ratio of 0.09.
capital_allocation.quote: On a gross basis, the borrowings are INR1,900 crores, but on a net basis, it is less than INR1,000 crores, to be precise, INR973 crores. If we consider net borrowing, the debt ratio is only 0.09, which is less than 0.1.

capital_allocation.claim: The Board recommended a final dividend of INR54 per share, making the total dividend for the year INR62 per share.
capital_allocation.quote: During the year, for the first time, CPCL paid an interim dividend, and we are happy to announce that in addition to the interim dividend of INR8 per equity share of INR10 each, the Board has recommended a final dividend of INR54 per share, taking the total dividend for the year to INR62 per share, which again is highest ever.

capital_allocation.claim: Total capex for the financial year was INR856 crores compared to INR673 crores in the previous year.
capital_allocation.quote: During the current year, the capex was INR856 crores as compared to INR673 crores in the previous year.

capital_allocation.claim: As of March 31, 2025, total debt stood at an absolute level of Rs. 3,100 crores and net worth was at Rs. 7,939 crores.
capital_allocation.quote: At an absolute level, the debt stands at Rs. 3,100 crores as compared to Rs. 2,762 crores as on March 31, 2024. Net worth is at Rs. 7,939 crores as on March 31, 2025.

risks_headwinds.claim: Management noted that uncertainties due to logistical constraints and volatility of crude oil prices pose challenges.
risks_headwinds.quote: Now with all this, I would like to say the uncertainties due to logistical constraints, volatility of crude oil prices do pose challenges.

risks_headwinds.claim: Uncertainties due to the volatility of crude prices pose a challenge to operations.
risks_headwinds.quote: Finally, the uncertainties due to volatility of crude prices do pose a challenge.

risks_headwinds.claim: CST under recovery was 463 Crore in 2022-23, 361 Crore in 2023-24, and 246 Crore in 9M 2024-25.

management_commitments.claim: The company expects the INR2,000 crores capex for the LOBS and retail outlet projects to be deployed over 2 to 3 years.
management_commitments.quote: This INR2,000 crores will happen over 2 to 3 years.

management_commitments.claim: Management estimates normal maintenance capex of approximately INR500 crores every year.
management_commitments.quote: Besides, every year, you can assume another INR500 crores is our normal capex.

management_commitments.claim: Normal maintenance capex for the next two years is projected to be around Rs. 250 to Rs. 300 crores per year.
management_commitments.quote: The normal maintenance CAPEX for the next two years would be around Rs. 250 to Rs. 300 crores, maintenance CAPEX plus small regular CAPEX normally.

_meta.note: Facts are verbatim-grounded against the company's own documents; claims whose quote was not found were dropped.
